description: Hi! I'm Sandipan, an AI/ML B.Tech student at HIT forming TEAM PRATISMRITI for the 'Abandoned but not Forgotten' challenge. Our goal is to blend data and storytelling to explore NASA's discarded lunar/martian tech.
summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive educational platform dedicated to preserving the stories of NASA’s discarded and retired spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars. While these machines have completed their active missions, they remain silent monuments of human curiosity, engineering triumph, and scientific discovery. Our project transforms these forgotten space artifacts into accessible, engaging experiences for learners, educators, and space enthusiasts. By combining historical mission archives, spatial data, and storytelling, users can explore the exact locations, technical milestones, and lasting scientific legacies of iconic hardware—from Apollo lunar modules to Mars rovers. Our goal is to bridge the gap between past space exploration and public awareness, ensuring that every mission's contribution to humanity's journey beyond Earth is remembered, celebrated, and used to inspire future generations of explorers.
details: Abandoned but not Forgotten: NASA's Relics Across the Cosmos" is an interactive 3D WebGL and web-based educational platform that tracks and tells the stories of discarded, retired, and silent space hardware left behind across the solar system since the 1960s. The platform features real-time orbital trajectory calculations, interactive telemetry data, and engaging narratives for iconic spacecraft, rovers, and landers such as Voyager 1 & 2, Pioneer 10 & 11,Apollo lunar modules, and Mars rovers. Users can navigate through deep space, the Moon, and Mars to uncover the technical milestones and scientific legacy behind each machine. The project bridges the gap between complex space archives and public awareness by transforming dense telemetry and historical technical records into an immersive, beginner-friendly experience, sparking curiosity and inspiring school-age students, educators, and space enthusiasts to explore STEM fields and space science. Developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, WebGL, Three.js, official NASA historical archives, and design tools like Canva, ChatGPT, and Gemini AI, the project carefully prioritizes accessibility to ensure that complex scientific concepts and orbital data are presented in a simple, engaging, and 100% free open-access format for learners of all ages.
